narrative.overview:
The whole system is one object: the printed-and-pencilled chart pinned in an Indian school's transport office. Cool bond paper, graphite print, duplicator blue for every rule and fill, pencil for the hand that corrects the print, one red pen kept for the exception, and the yellow of the bus itself - on every vehicle marker, on a cell whose trip is running, and as the highlighter over one line of a headline. Nothing in the interface is made of a material that is not on that desk - no gradient, no glass, no card floating in space.

Its grammar is a grid, not a page. Rows are routes; columns are the day's four moments. Every surface in the product is assembled from one ruled cell in four states - printed (not yet happened), pencilled (happening now, written over the print), filled (done, inked), struck (marked in red pen) - and from one pinned sheet with a heavy frame and a printed header band. That is why the landing hero, the admin dashboard, the driver's thumb-sized roster and a parent's single row all read as the same chart at different magnifications: admin is the whole chart, the driver PWA is one column of it, a parent sees one row, their child's day.

The build is light-only on purpose. There is no dark mode and no theme switch, because the two real use scenes are a desk in daylight and a driver's phone in sunlight; a dark sheet would be a category habit, not a reading of either. Density is high and even: information is set in tabular type at a size you can read across a desk, and the chart never softens a fact to make a screen calmer.
keyCharacteristics: Five materials only: paper, graphite, duplicator blue, pencil, one red pen.
Square corners everywhere; zero border-radius in the entire interface.
Every rule is a 1px or 2px line, never a shadow or a gap.
Machine-read facts (codes, times, counts, registrations) are typewriter-set and tabular.
Light-only, chosen from the use scene: daylight desk, sunlit windscreen.
One authored motion: the chart writes itself left to right.

rules.name: The Red Pen Rule
rules.body: Red marks one thing: a child who is not on the bus (or the system's inability to send that fact). It is never a brand accent, never a destructive-button colour by habit, never decoration. If a screen shows red and no child is unaccounted for, the red is wrong.

rules.name: The Five Materials Rule
rules.body: Paper, graphite, duplicator blue, pencil, red pen. A new surface may not introduce a sixth colour. Semantic states that are not "exception" are expressed with the blue tints and the paper bands, not with green, amber, or purple.

rules.name: The Daylight Rule
rules.body: Light-only. No dark mode, no theme toggle, no prefers-color-scheme branch. The product is read on a daylit desk and through a sunlit windscreen; contrast is tuned for glare, not for a dark room.

rules.name: The Typewriter Rule
rules.body: If a value came off a clock, a tap, a form field or a database row, it is set in Courier Prime with tabular numerals. If it came off a writer, it is set in Archivo. Never mix the two inside one string.

rules.name: The Narrow Caps Rule
rules.body: Every heading and every label is Archivo Narrow, bold or semibold, uppercase. Sentence-case headings do not exist in this system; the chart's titles were printed, not written.

rules.name: The Ruled Cell Rule
rules.body: New surfaces are composed from the existing Cell and Sheet, in one of the four cell states. A new surface that needs a container does not get a new container; it gets a sheet.

rules.name: The Thumb Column Rule
rules.body: Any driver-facing surface is one column at max-w-md, with tap targets at least 3.75rem tall and the primary action pinned to the bottom edge.

rules.name: The Pinned Sheet Rule
rules.body: One shadow, one owner. Only .chart casts. Anything else that wants separation gets a rule, a tonal band, or nothing.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: No border-radius. If a shape needs to feel softer, it gets more padding, not a curve.

rules.name: The One Stroke Rule
rules.body: Every icon is drawn at 1.6 stroke weight in currentColor, inline SVG. The set is closed; a new glyph is drawn to match, never imported.

rules.name: The Yellow Rule
rules.body: Yellow is the bus, or it is live, or it is the highlighter run over the one line on a page that matters. It is never a brand accent, never a warning, never a third status colour. A yellow cell means that trip is running right now; a yellow marker on a map is a vehicle.

dos: Do build every new surface out of Sheet and Cell in one of the four states; the chart is the layout, not a widget inside it.
Do reserve red (#C62B1F) for a child who is not on the bus, and nothing else.
Do set every machine-produced value - time, count, code, registration - in Courier Prime with tabular numerals.
Do separate things with a ruled line: hairline blue-3 inside a sheet, mid blue-2 for a real column division, 2px blue for a frame or header edge.
Do keep every corner square and every icon at 1.6 stroke weight in currentColor.
Do size driver surfaces for a thumb in sunlight: one max-w-md column, rows at least 3.75rem tall, the primary action pinned to the bottom edge.
Do keep prose measures in ch (42-62ch) and headings balanced and short.
donts: Don't add a sixth material. No green "success", no amber "warning", no purple accent; state is expressed in the blue tints and paper bands.
Don't add a dark mode or a theme toggle. Light-only is a decision about the desk and the windscreen.
Don't give anything but .chart a shadow, and never use a shadow where a rule will do.
Don't round a corner, anywhere, including map pins and badges.
Don't put a gutter or gap between cells inside a sheet; adjacent cells share a rule.
Don't animate anything other than the cell write-in and the 0.15s button colour transition.
Don't import an icon set or use a glyph/emoji as an icon; draw it into the existing stroke set.
Don't set a heading in Archivo (body) or a code in Archivo Narrow; the three faces have fixed jobs.
